text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu: No building on Ras al-Amoud.
- Paul Volcker opposes class action lawsuits on dormant Holocaust accounts.
- Palestinian President Arafat expected to shake up cabinet.
- Netanyahu suspicious of United States response to his refusal to freeze settlements.
- U.S. Jewish businessmen Moskowitz resolute to build in Ras al-Amoud; prime minister makes clear he'll fight the plan.
- Prime minister blasts 1998 Treasury forecast as "too pessimistic".
- Israel: we'll capture every terrorist released by the Palestinian Authority like we did in Tulkarm.
- Netanyahu to Maariv: We'll prevent the building in Ras al-Amoud. Moskowitz to Maariv: it's impossible to stop us.
- Claridge proposes purchase of Bank Leumi's Koor shares.
- Netanyahu promised Arafat: We won't build the neighbourhood. Arafat: This time I believe Netanyahu.
